turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
The strongest candidates combine selective, low-recombination oxide ETLs with high-quality hole extraction and well-matched metal contacts:

1. **c005** — The TiO₂/PCBM bilayer should improve electron extraction and passivate the perovskite/oxide interface. Its PCDTBT/MoO₃/Au hole-contact stack closely matches a 19.35% training configuration.
2. **c068** — SnO₂/TiO₂ provides favorable electron-energy cascading and good hole blocking, while PTAA is among the best-performing HTLs in the training data. Au/MoO₃ should further reduce hole-contact losses.
3. **c083** — Dimethylbiguanide is likely an ultrathin TiO₂/perovskite interfacial modifier: its Lewis-basic groups can passivate under-coordinated Pb and suppress nonradiative recombination, while Spiro-MeOTAD/Au supplies a reliable selective contact.
4. **c017** — The C60-based electron contact and F6-TCNNQ-doped TaTm hole stack are highly selective. The nearly identical Au-contact training device reaches 17.9%; Ag may introduce a small work-function and stability penalty.
5. **c064** — A TiO₂/SnO₂ nanoparticle ETL combines effective hole blocking with improved interfacial passivation. A close Ag-contact training analogue reaches 17.47%, and Au is chemically compatible with Spiro-MeOTAD.

**Final: c005, c068, c083, c017, c064**
